approachQuestion.prompt:
A string uses symbols numbered 0 through k-1. Return the length of its longest contiguous substring in which every symbol appears an even number of times. The empty substring is allowed.

Constraints: 1 <= k <= 10; 2^k <= n <= 200000; string length is n.
Example: k=2, symbols=[0,1,0,1] -> 4. Example: k=2, [0,0,1,0] -> 2.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: k is a parameter despite its practical cap. One word holds a k-bit mask. Bit operations and array accesses cost constant time; initializing all 2^k table entries is charged.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: Store the earliest prefix index for each parity mask in a direct table, initially mask zero at prefix index 0. Toggle the current symbol bit per character; compare the current prefix index with the earliest index for this mask.
options.feedback: Equal prefix parity masks mean their intervening substring has even counts for every symbol. The earliest matching prefix gives the longest ending here.

options.text: Store a list of all prefix indices per mask; after the scan, use last minus first in each list.
options.feedback: First and last occurrences give the right length, but storing middle occurrences is unnecessary.

options.text: Find the longest substring whose parity mask has at most one set bit.
options.feedback: That permits one odd count. For k=1 and [0,0,0], it returns 3 instead of the required 2.

options.text: If all full-string counts are even, return n; otherwise return zero.
options.feedback: A proper substring can satisfy the rule. For k=2 and [0,0,1,0], the correct answer is 2, not zero.

feedback.reason: Equal prefix parity masks mean every intervening symbol count is even.
details: Keep a parity mask for the prefix and the first prefix index at which each mask occurred. Toggle one bit for each new symbol. Repeated masks delimit an all-even substring; compare their index distance and retain the maximum.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For earliest-equal-parity, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the string length and k the alphabet size. Recall n >= 2^k.
constraints: k is a parameter despite its practical cap. One word holds a k-bit mask. Bit operations and array accesses cost constant time; initializing all 2^k table entries is charged.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: Initialize 2^k earliest positions, then toggle one bit per character.
details: Table initialization costs 2^k and the scan costs n, giving O(n) under n >= 2^k. The direct table occupies 2^k words; only earliest indices are kept.
k is a parameter despite its practical cap. One word holds a k-bit mask. Bit operations and array accesses cost constant time; initializing all 2^k table entries is charged.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The earliest-index table has an entry for every parity mask.
“O(n²) time, O(2^k) auxiliary space”: Only one table lookup and update are needed per character.
“O(nk) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The fixed method toggles a mask bit instead of recounting each symbol.
